results.claim: THEORY.md, R1. The pure integrated-coordinate order cannot be lowered

human: Gilbert–Kuo–Sloan, distribution functions and densities, Theorem 3, arXiv:2112.10308v5
comparison.explanation: Optimality side of A-GKLS: for every retained mixed order with sum at least two, even one fewer phase derivative in the integrated coordinate can invalidate the original joint conclusion, while all available weighted input and trace hypotheses hold. This is a necessity result, not a better sufficient bound.

coordinates.class: Gaussian unit-jump integrands with one regular graph, strictly monotone phase with partial derivative at least 1, all retained phase orders and all finite Gaussian moments
inputs: Exact preintegration in the stated coordinate
coordinates.bound: With q integrated-coordinate phase derivatives and retained target order r of sum greater than q, the preintegral is C^q but no ordered retained partial of total order q+1 can be everywhere defined and continuous; in particular the target classical mixed class is not guaranteed.
coordinates.validity: All m retained dimensions and integer 1 <= q < sum(r), including q = sum(r)-1; all finite Gaussian Lp input exponents
coordinates.guarantee: Exact pointwise regularity obstruction, not a quadrature or query-rate bound

results.claim: THEORY.md, R2. The mixed weak L2 condition itself can fail

human: Gilbert–Kuo–Sloan, distribution functions and densities, Theorem 3, arXiv:2112.10308v5
comparison.explanation: Optimality side of A-GKLS at retained order (1,1) and p=2. Even discarding the classical conclusion does not rescue the weak mixed L2 guarantee when the phase order is lowered to one.

coordinates.class: Three-dimensional Gaussian unit jumps with one regular graph and integrated phase derivative in [1/2,1]; all retained phase derivatives and all applicable boundary factors controlled
inputs: Exact preintegration in the stated coordinate
Explicit inverse phase profile and constant amplitude
coordinates.bound: Output is C^1, but every locally integrable representative of its weak mixed second derivative fails square integrability on [-1,1]^2 and in the product Gaussian measure
coordinates.validity: d=3, integrated phase order one and target retained order (1,1); p=2 for the failed output condition
coordinates.guarantee: Exact local and Gaussian weak-regularity obstruction
